mutations.before:
*)
      printf '%s\n' "gate: unknown profile: $PROFILE — known profiles: $(known_profiles)" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
mutations.because: the refusal of an unknown profile name. Answered by running the default gate instead, a caller who typed `--profile midnigth` gets a run that filtered nothing, at vitest's default 5s timeout, with coverage thresholds ENFORCED rather than the caveat a profile prints — a green gate under a name that promised a filtered one, and the promise is the only thing the host had to go on. Nothing downstream can notice: the step list is built from `[ -n "$PROFILE" ]`, so clearing the variable is invisible downstream and the run is byte-for-byte the default gate. The test asserts exit 2, that the refusal names midnight so it is an answer rather than a shrug, and that the injected step never ran (CF_GATE_STEPS is a single `true`), which is what turns a fall-through from a slow real-suite failure into a fast assertion failure
command: an unknown profile is refused, not run as the default gate

mutations.before:
[ -n "$2" ] || { printf '%s\n' "gate: invalid profile name: (empty) — must match ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\$" >&2; exit 2; }
      PROFILE="$2"
mutations.because: the refusal of an EMPTY --profile value. Answered by accepting it, which is the same fall-through the unknown-profile refusal exists to stop: every check after the parse loop reads an empty PROFILE as no profile at all, so `--profile ''` runs the DEFAULT gate — filtering nothing, at vitest's default 5s timeout, with coverage thresholds ENFORCED instead of the caveat a profile prints — and `--profile midnight --profile ''` resets a real profile to that, because the last flag is the one that counts. The empty string is not exotic input, it is what an unset shell variable interpolates to (`--profile "$PROFILE_NAME"`, a CI matrix cell, a wrapper script), and nothing on the way there says a profile was dropped. The test asserts exit 2, that the refusal says `invalid profile name`, and that the injected step never ran (CF_GATE_STEPS is a single `true`) — for the bare empty value AND for a real profile overridden by an empty one, so a mutant that silently resets to the default gate fails in about a second on an assertion instead of on a 13-step real suite
command: a --profile without a value, and one that is not a name, are refused

mutations.because: the exclusion listing's filter, back to a hand-written literal. The listing is the one line that tells a reader which tests a green run did NOT run, and it is derived from the profile's own filter — negated as a group, `!(!golden-bytes && !cpu-bound)` — precisely so it cannot name a different set than the one the test step runs. Restored to its own `'golden-bytes || cpu-bound'`, the two become independent again, and the next host fact breaks the banner silently: midnight gains a third tag (a slower rasterizer, another fixed internal deadline) and the gate filters it out correctly — the step's filter is the one vitest applies, so the RUN is right and stays green — while the "EXCLUDES" block keeps listing only the two old tests. The reader is then told this run skipped five tests when it skipped six, and the tests the new tag covers do not appear anywhere in the output that exists to name them. Nothing fails today, and nothing would fail later: the literal happens to select the same five tests now, the listing is deliberately non-fatal so a collection problem cannot fail a test step, and every profiled case injects CF_GATE_LIST_EXCLUDED, so no existing test ever resolved the default command this mutation restores. The test resolves that default through the profile itself (CF_GATE_TEST_PRINT_LISTING reports the command instead of running it), reads the test step's own `--tagsFilter` out of `--print-steps`, and asserts the listing is the exact complement of it — same tag set, one negated as a group — for every profile the script knows, read from its PROFILES list so a second profile is covered without editing the test. So the mutant is a one-line string mismatch, in about a second, on a `true` step: no collection, no lock, no suite.
command: the exclusion listing is derived from the profile's own filter, not a second list of tags
